decisions.quote: We found conflict adaptation (averaged across task repetitions and task switches) to be enhanced in negative mood. We did not replicate our previous finding of enhanced conflict adaptation in task switches in positive mood.
decisions.reason: Under Codebook Rule 2, outcome coding when no overall verdict is stated relies strictly on explicit or implicit comparisons to original findings established in the supplied source text, and stated outcomes must not be withheld because only the abstract is available. The supplied source explicitly states one comparison to Schuch and Pütz (2018)—'We did not replicate our previous finding of enhanced conflict adaptation in task switches in positive mood'—and does not establish any other specific original finding against which the negative-mood result can be compared under Rule 2(a). Because the sole source-established comparison to the original study failed to replicate, the outcome on the supplied text is 'failed'.

scope_review.parent_objection: First reply returns undeterminable because a positive-mood original effect failed while new negative-mood result is not linked to original. Codebook Rule2 compares only source-established original findings; source explicitly says We did not replicate our previous finding of enhanced conflict adaptation in task switches in positive mood. Does this directly establish failed for the named original finding, rather than withhold because unseen full text could contain other components? Inspect whole source including title and abstract. Do not infer mixed from the new negative-mood result unless source states it was original finding; do not withhold a stated original failure solely because supplied evidence is an abstract. Distinguish genuine overall verdict versus specific finding and identify whether any other actual original comparison is supported.

prior_reply.quote: We found conflict adaptation (averaged across task repetitions and task switches) to be enhanced in negative mood. We did not replicate our previous finding of enhanced conflict adaptation in task switches in positive mood.
prior_reply.reason: The abstract explicitly reports failing to replicate the positive-mood task-switch effect while finding enhanced conflict adaptation in negative mood, but does not state whether the negative-mood or within-task result replicated another component of Schuch and Pütz (2018). Because the source is abstract-only and the shipped quote comes from unseen full text, the available text neither confirms a mixed outcome nor rules out a replicated component in the full text.
